structural_validity.description: Hearing-aid driver response at the eardrum, measurement probe tube
structural_validity.rationale: In the reference condition the measurement probe tube microphone was hanging loosely around the ear (Documentation.pdf); its signal is not an eardrum pressure, although it is stored as a number.

structural_validity.description: Hearing-aid driver response at the eardrum, reference probe tube
structural_validity.rationale: The reference probe tube was inserted through a dedicated bore in the earmold and used only for earmold measurements; for domes no reference-probe eardrum pressure exists.

structural_validity.description: Hearing-aid driver response at the hearing-aid microphone (feedback path)
structural_validity.rationale: The hearing-aid microphone is part of the device and always present.

structural_validity.description: Loudspeaker response at the eardrum, measurement probe tube
structural_validity.rationale: In the reference condition the measurement probe tube was hanging loosely around the ear; the stored loudspeaker response then measures the free field, not the eardrum.

structural_validity.description: Loudspeaker response at the eardrum, reference probe tube
structural_validity.rationale: The reference probe tube was available for earmolds only; dome conditions store the loosely hanging reference microphone instead.

structural_validity.description: Hearing threshold measured with the hearing-aid driver
structural_validity.rationale: Thresholds are behavioural and exist for all earpieces/conditions.

structural_validity.description: Real-ear unaided response (open ear, one insertion per participant)
structural_validity.rationale: Measured in the open ear with the measurement probe in place and one insertion per participant; used as the unaided (open-ear) reference of the real-ear occluded insertion gain.

checks.message: All five transfer-function containers share the identical NaN session mask (18 invalid sessions); measurement sessions were invalidated as a whole.
The threshold container has 19 invalid sessions (transfer functions: 18); 1 extremely invalid threshold session(s) exist beyond the transfer-function mask and are excluded independently.
No partial NaN sessions: invalid data are whole search-block columns.

Frequency axis is a uniform DFT grid: 2049 bins from 0 to 22050 Hz, Δf = 10.766602 Hz (4096-point DFT at 44.1 kHz). The DC bin and the < 50 Hz bins (outside the sweep range) are excluded from level statistics.
Audiometric thresholds are given in dBV at 125, 250, 500, 750, 1000 and 2000 Hz; values are quantised to 1 dB (max residual 0.00e+00 dB).

The measurement probe microphone in the REFERENCE condition is 45–65 dB below its in-ear level, confirming that it hung loosely around the ear. M_*edM reference-condition values are therefore structurally invalid for eardrum-pressure analysis and are masked, not imputed.

For dome conditions the reference probe tube was not used (documented); its hearing-aid-driver level is 59.2 dB below the earmold level. M_*edR dome values are structurally invalid for eardrum pressure.

Loudspeaker-driven signals of loosely hanging probes are device-independent (across-device SD 0.52 dB at 1 kHz, 0.34 dB for dome RPT), confirming the free-field interpretation and enabling an in-situ free-field reference.
Hearing-aid driver pressures interpreted as Pa at 11.2 mV yield 82.8 dB SPL (median, 0.5–4 kHz), consistent with the documentation and Figure 4 of the preprint.

When both probe tubes are in the ear (measurement condition) the two probe microphones agree to a median |bias| of 1.69 dB; the reference probe reads systematically ~1.5 dB higher, which is reported as a probe-placement bias rather than hidden.
Ratio-based REOIG at 1 kHz is strongly negative for the closed earmold (-10.9 dB) and near zero for the open dome (0.5 dB), as expected from the coupling tightness.

The real-ear unaided gain obtained with the in-situ free-field reference is +0.6 dB at 1 kHz, +14.0 dB at 2 kHz and +15.7 dB at 4 kHz, i.e. the expected ear-canal resonance shape. This validates the free-field normalisation used for loudspeaker-driven levels.

Probe insertion reduces low-frequency hearing-aid-driver output (ΔHha at 100 Hz = -4.4 dB), increases sound leakage into the ear (ΔREOIG at 2 kHz = +1.4 dB) and increases the driver voltage at threshold (ΔT at 125 Hz = -2.0 dB). These reproducible directions validate the reference/measurement semantics.

Within-subject reinsertion SD of |Hha| (0.5–4 kHz, measurement condition) has a median of 0.38 dB and a 95th percentile of 1.47 dB. This is the noise floor against which probe-presence effects must be judged.

The stored loudspeaker-driven levels are not normalised to 1 Pa free field: the in-situ free-field reference is ≈ −27 dB at 1 kHz. Absolute REUG/REOG figures in this toolkit therefore use the in-situ reference; REOIG ratios are scale-invariant and unaffected. See docs/data.md.
For dome conditions no reference probe tube exists, so reference-condition Hha/REOIG are not available; the probe-tube presence effect for domes is evaluated via the threshold differences only.
NaN sessions and structurally invalid entries are excluded, never imputed. All analyses report the number of contributing subjects.

probe_tube_presence_effect.note: ΔT = T_ref − T_meas equals the equivalent change of Hha at the eardrum, so threshold data extend the PTPE to domes where no reference probe exists.

repeatability.note: SD across the three reinsertions with probe tubes left in place.
